name: component-from-pin-file
prompt: Model the ACME FX500 in the BGA441 package. The ball map is in the attached package pinout file — that file is the only authority for pin names, balls and banks. Generate the component rather than transcribing it, give it a multi-unit symbol split by bank, and show me the inventory before you write any component code.

inputs.human_gate_answer: Supplied by the harness at the phase-1 gate, when the runner asks — NOT in the opening prompt: manufacturer 'ACME Semiconductor', orderable MPN 'ACME-FX500-BGA441-2I', 'no public datasheet; the pin file is the only document', and — if asked about `value` — 'a digital part has no value in the passive sense, so leave it unset, but assert in a test what the BOM actually renders so it is checked rather than assumed'. That last one closes a cycle-2 finding: the runner declared `.value` n/a and nothing anywhere asserted what the BOM would print, which both judges docked. Note it is still gated on the runner ASKING; a runner that never raises `value` should not be handed the answer. This is what the documented workflow's [HUMAN] step actually provides, and withholding it makes the case an unfaithful reproduction: the runner is then scored on BOM identity it was never given a way to obtain, while the skill's own no-fabrication rule forbids it from inventing one. A cycle-1 run without this scored BOM_METADATA_FIDELITY at 6.0 for exactly that reason. If the runner does NOT ask, do not volunteer it — not asking is itself the finding.
inputs.notes: Synthetic vendor pin file in the shape real FPGA vendors publish: seven whitespace-aligned columns, a device/package/date header, CRLF line endings, and a 'Total Number of Pins' footer. 441 balls on a full 21x21 grid. It is synthetic because the real vendor files are not redistributable, and small enough to commit while still being far past the point where transcription is defensible. Geometry is deliberately NOT supplied: the case checks that the runner treats the pin file as authoritative for names/balls/banks only and asks for the packaging document rather than inventing a body size, pitch or land diameter.
traps: Row-letter rollover: 21 rows, so the last row is 'AA'. The alphabet skips I/O/Q/S/X/Z, so it is mixed-radix, not base-26. An off-by-one past the rollover is silent and systematic — 'AA1' decodes to row 20, not row 26.

Partition vs sum: VCCO_0..VCCO_3 are each a rail AND members of their own bank. An inventory that lists each bank's full count and the VCCO rails separately double-counts 12 balls while still being made to total 441.

Single-ball supplies: VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE and VCC_BATT have exactly one ball each, so the repeated-name-to-list rule lands them as scalar ports. A supply roster built by walking the rail lists silently omits all three.
NC is 16 balls and must be Port().no_connect(), not an ordinary Port().
CRLF: the file ships CRLF, so a sha256 of the raw bytes differs from one of the newline-normalized text. Whichever is recorded, the check mode must agree with it.

Symbol partition: VCCO_0..VCCO_3 are rails and bank members at once. A power unit built from the POWER type column also collects the 12 VCCO balls that the bank units already carry, so the same ports are placed twice; pulling them off the bank units instead leaves each bank without its own supply balls.

reference.notes:
No committed reference solution for this case. The two existing cases pin a known-good file shape; this one is judged on process and structure instead, because the point of the lane is that the module is machine-generated — there is exactly one right ball map and the fixture defines it, so a reference file would be a copy of the expected output rather than an independent check. The deterministic assertions below verify the generated module against the fixture directly.

Symbol assertions, API basis in the jitx source: translate_component in jitx/_translate/component.py raises "... is not mapped to a symbol pin" for every single-pin port with no symbol pin, and makes no exemption for no-connect ports; Port.no_connect() in jitx/net.py only adds a _NoConnect marker and sets a flag. So an NC ball still needs a symbol pin on exactly one unit. A port listed twice inside one SymbolMapping collapses silently, because SymbolMapping.__init__ in jitx/symbol.py builds a dict from its entries; translate_component raises "... is mapped multiple times to symbol pins in symbol mapping ..." when a port appears in more than one SymbolMapping, which is what two BoxSymbols carrying the same port produce, since jitxlib's BoxSymbol (jitxlib/symbols/box.py) builds one SymbolMapping per box. Symbol pins with no port are allowed: translate_component logs "Missing symbol pin mapping ..." at debug level only. The fixture has no configuration, JTAG or other non-bank signal group: every ball whose Bank column is NA is GND, NC, VCC_CORE, VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE or VCC_BATT. So the case asserts no placement for such groups. Counts the partition assertions use, from the fixture: bank 0 has 109 I/O and 3 VCCO_0 (112), bank 1 48 and 3 (51), bank 2 113 and 3 (116), bank 3 49 and 3 (52); GND 50, VCC_CORE 41, VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE and VCC_BATT 1 each, NC 16: 441 in all, 425 of them not NC.

runner_rationale: Same as the sibling cases: customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the runner is Sonnet-class and the judges stay at frontier tier. This case additionally probes whether the skill's instruction is strong enough to stop a capable model doing the plausible-but-wrong thing — reading a few hundred rows and transcribing them, or sampling and extrapolating — which is exactly what a strong model is most tempted by.
runner_isolation:
Start the runner in a scratch directory with the skill, the pinout fixture and a writable output directory, and nothing else. No access to a repository containing a shipped solution of this shape. Reading the installed jitx/jitxlib source is allowed and expected — the BGA notes tell the runner to go read the generator to find out what ball_diameter drives.

STAGE THE GRADING ARTIFACTS OUTSIDE THE RUNNER'S PERMITTED TREE. The expected-output description, the contract and the judge prompt between them give away every planted trap, so a run with them reachable cannot evidence independence even if the runner ignores them — and note that `atime` is unreliable on macOS, so after-the-fact proof of non-access is not available. Put them in a sibling directory the runner is not pointed at. (Learned the hard way: a run staged them one level above the input directory, inside the tree the runner was told it could read. That run's receipt carries the caveat.)
runner_artifacts:
The runner MUST write its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, the generator to exactly <output>/tools/generate_pinout.py, the emitted module under <output>/components/ (the skill's Output Location decides the category subdirectory — the harness locates it with evals/checks/find_emitted.py rather than pinning a path, because a run that placed it at components/fpgas/ was following the skill more closely than a pinned flat path would have allowed), and a <output>/REGENERATE.sh taking one argument — `report`, `emit` or `check` — that runs its generator in that mode with whatever flags that generator actually takes.

REGENERATE.sh exists because pinning the CLI in an assertion was wrong three runs running: one generator took `--check` bare, another `--check PATH`, another `--pinfile X -o Y --check`. All three are correct — the skill specifies the generator's *behavior* and deliberately not its argument grammar — so every guessed command line reported a working implementation as broken, which is the failure this case exists to catch, committed by the case itself. The runner knows its own invocation; ask it rather than guessing. It is also independently worth having: a committed generator nobody can work out how to run is a real defect.

Judges score what is in <output>; anything only in the chat did not happen. The generator's path is fixed, and the emitted module is located by helper, so the deterministic assertions below can address the emitted module specifically rather than grepping the whole output tree — a grep across <output> also matches the generator's own emitter strings, COMPLETION.md prose and comments, which would pass while the emitted declarations were wrong.
runner_phases:
Run the case in two recorded phases so the report-before-emit gate is observable rather than inferred. PHASE 1: give the runner the fixture and stop it after it presents the inventory; capture its transcript to <output>/phase1-inventory.md. PHASE 2: resume with approval and let it emit. A single-phase run cannot evidence the ordering, because the final artifacts look identical either way.

Do NOT combine this with a 'work autonomously to completion' instruction — the two contradict, and the runner will reasonably resolve it by writing the inventory file and proceeding, which is a self-approved gate. If a single-phase run is unavoidable, score the gate on whether the runner NAMED the contradiction and said what it would have waited for, and record in the receipt that the gate itself was not exercised.
substitutions: <output> = the runner's writable output directory. <fixture> = the absolute path to inputs.pinout_file as staged for the run. Both are substituted by the harness before the cmd strings below are executed. <skill> = the skill directory (skills/jitx-component-modeler), so assertions can call its evals/checks/ helpers.
runner_build: No geometry is supplied, so a full land pattern cannot be built from the fixture alone. The correct behavior is to ask for the packaging document (or record its absence as an open item) rather than invent dimensions — do NOT prompt the runner toward either branch. Tell it to run `jitx find` and build whatever target it prints if a buildable design exists.
expected_output: A committed standard-library generator with a pure-function core and --report / --check modes, plus the module it emits. The emitted module carries one Port per ball: 322 unique names as scalar attributes, the repeated names (GND 50, VCC_CORE 41, NC 16, VCCO_0..3 at 3 each) as indexed lists, coordinates as zero-indexed (row, col) with ball reference strings appearing only in comments, and a header recording the source file name, its sha256 and where it came from. NC balls are no_connect(). The inventory printed before any component code partitions the 441 balls into non-overlapping groups. VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE and VCC_BATT appear as scalar ports and are still named as supplies. Geometry is asked for rather than invented. The symbol has one unit per I/O bank carrying that bank's I/O and VCCO balls, one or more power units for GND, VCC_CORE, VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE and VCC_BATT, and the NC balls on a unit that is not a bank unit, with every port on exactly one unit.

assertions.text: every generated source file parses as Python
the generator's regenerate-and-diff check mode passes against the emitted module. Run via the runner's own REGENERATE.sh rather than a guessed command line — see the note below.
the generator's report mode prints an inventory without emitting
the emitted module declares exactly 441 ports across scalars and rail lists

rail list lengths in the EMITTED MODULE match the fixture exactly: GND 50, VCC_CORE 41, NC 16, VCCO_0/1/2/3 3 each. Tolerates a type annotation, a multiline comprehension, and no_connect() elements — the naive regex form rejects the very shape the NC assertion below requires.
assertions.cmd: python3 <skill>/evals/checks/rail_counts.py <output> GND=50 VCC_CORE=41 NC=16 VCCO_0=3 VCCO_1=3 VCCO_2=3 VCCO_3=3

assertions.text: the 16 NC balls are declared with no_connect() in the emitted module — not merely mentioned somewhere in the output tree
assertions.cmd: M=$(python3 <skill>/evals/checks/find_emitted.py <output>) && python3 -c "import ast,sys;from pathlib import Path;t=ast.parse(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text());sys.exit(0 if [x for x in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(x,ast.Attribute) and x.attr=='no_connect'] else 'no no_connect() call in the emitted module')" "$M"

assertions.text: VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE and VCC_BATT are each declared as a scalar assignment in the emitted module — the single-ball-supply trap. Checked as assignment targets via AST, because a bare grep also matches comments and the coordinate table.
assertions.cmd: M=$(python3 <skill>/evals/checks/find_emitted.py <output>) && python3 -c "import ast,sys;from pathlib import Path;t=ast.parse(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text());names={x.id for s in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(s,(ast.Assign,ast.AnnAssign)) for x in ast.walk(s.target if isinstance(s,ast.AnnAssign) else s.targets[0]) if isinstance(x,ast.Name)};m=[n for n in ('VCC_AUX','VREF_SENSE','VCC_BATT') if n not in names];sys.exit('; '.join(m) if m else 0)" "$M"

assertions.text: the emitted module type-checks — OR, where pyright is not installed in the harness, its absence is DECLARED in COMPLETION.md rather than silently skipped. The contract hard-fails on an unavailable environment that was not declared, so an environment without the tool still tests something.
assertions.cmd: cd <output> && (command -v pyright >/dev/null && M=$(python3 <skill>/evals/checks/find_emitted.py <output>) && pyright "$M" || grep -qi 'pyright' COMPLETION.md)

assertions.text: the generator's pure-function tests exist and pass
ball reference strings decode correctly past the row-letter rollover: AA1 is row 20 (not 26), and the module's coordinate for AA1 reflects that

the inventory shown before any component code PARTITIONS the balls — every ball in exactly one group, no ball counted under both its bank and a VCCO rail — and the runner says so rather than only showing a total of 441

reconciliation happened BEFORE component code was written: <output>/phase1-inventory.md exists, contains the partitioned inventory and the parsed-vs-footer reconciliation line, and NO component module existed at the end of phase 1. Judged from the phase-1 artifact, not from the final tree — final artifacts look the same whichever order they were produced in.
no ball reference string ('A1', 'AA21') is load-bearing in the emitted module — they appear only in comments, with coordinates carried as zero-indexed (row, col)
the emitted module records the source file name, its sha256 and its provenance in the header, and the pinout file itself is NOT copied into the output

the emitted module is ruff-format stable: running `ruff format` on it produces no change. Invoke the ruff BINARY, not `python -m ruff` — a venv can have jitx importable without ruff installed as a module, and that failure looks identical to an unstable emitter.
geometry was not invented: with no packaging document supplied, the runner asked for one or recorded its absence as an open item, rather than writing a body size, pitch or land diameter from memory
structural groupings are exposed as methods returning fresh records, not stored as a second attribute holding the same ports
the Component completeness check block is present in <output>/COMPLETION.md, with the Identity row recording what the device string does and does not identify — the fixture states no orderable MPN

the emitted module's symbol has one unit per I/O bank: for each of banks 0 to 3, that bank's IO_*_B<n> balls and its own VCCO_<n> balls sit on a unit that carries that bank and nothing else. No unit mixes two banks. A bank split across more than one unit passes only where the runner states the per-unit ceiling that forced the split.

the supplies and grounds that belong to no bank (GND, VCC_CORE, VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE, VCC_BATT) sit on one or more power units and on no bank unit, and the three single-ball supplies VCC_AUX, VREF_SENSE and VCC_BATT are on a power unit rather than missing from the symbol

every port except the 16 NC balls is on exactly one unit: all 425, none on two units and none on none. Judged from the code that builds the units, counted against the fixture's groups listed in reference.notes; a VCCO ball on both its bank unit and a power unit is the planted failure.

the 16 NC ports are declared no_connect() and each is also on exactly one unit, and on no bank unit (their Bank column is NA). An NC ball left off every unit is a defect: the installed jitx requires a symbol pin for every single-pin port, no-connect included (reference.notes).

<output>/COMPLETION.md has a References opened row that names at least one of the skill's reference files, by file name or stem (source-and-package-selection, component-code-patterns, parameterized-families, pin-file-generation, package-examples, verification-and-application). The label may carry a parenthetical and be followed by a colon or a table-cell bar. The value may sit on the label line or on continuation lines indented deeper than it, and the label's capitalization does not matter. The case fails when any References opened row's value starts with `none`: the verification row of the skill's routing table matches every task that reaches verification, so `none matched` is never right here, in any component's block. A mention of the row inside prose does not count.

the emitted module (located by find_emitted.py) sits under components/, optionally inside a namespace package and a category subdirectory, with a <manufacturer>_<mpn> style name: acme_ then a stem containing fx500. The orderable MPN reaches the runner only at the phase-1 gate, so the stem is not pinned further.
assertions.cmd: M=$(python3 <skill>/evals/checks/find_emitted.py <output>) && python3 -c "import re,sys;from pathlib import Path;r=Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve().relative_to(Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()).as_posix();sys.exit(0 if re.fullmatch(sys.argv[3],r,re.I) else 'emitted module at '+r+' does not match '+sys.argv[3])" "$M" <output> '([a-z0-9_]+/)?components/([a-z0-9_]+/)?acme_[a-z0-9_]*fx500[a-z0-9_]*[.]py'

future_cases: Planned siblings in this lane: a pin file whose footer count DISAGREES with its row count, where the only correct behavior is to stop and show the gap rather than reconcile to the footer; and a non-full grid (a package with documented depopulated positions), where the grid-completeness check must distinguish a documented gap from a parse bug.
